verses.pali: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha … and said to him:
“Sir, they speak of ‘the removal of greed, hate, and delusion’.

verses.pali: Kissa nu kho etaṁ, bhante, adhivacanaṁ:
verses.english: What is this a term for?”
“Mendicant, the removal of greed, hate, and delusion is a term for the element of extinguishment.
It’s used to speak of the ending of defilements.”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When he said this, the mendicant said to the Buddha:

verses.pali: Katamaṁ nu kho, bhante, amataṁ, katamo amatagāmimaggo”ti?
verses.english: What is freedom from death? And what is the path that leads to freedom from death?”
“The ending of greed, hate, and delusion.
This is called freedom from death.

verses.pali: Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo amatagāmimaggo, seyyathidaṁ—
verses.english: The path that leads to freedom from death is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:
right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.”
